A signaller stands right out on the tower's open gallery with one arm straight up and the other straight out to the side, holding the position dead still, her whole body braced back against the wind and the city dropping away beneath her.

Two of a cable crew are out on a bosun's chair halfway across the gap between two towers, one hauling hand over hand on the traveller rope and the other paying out new wire from a coil on his knees, nothing but air underneath them.
A tower keeper is leaning back with both hands locked on a long crank handle and his shoulders right into it, walking a blade up through its arc one heave at a time.
A signaller is sitting inside the little cabin at the tower top with its door swung open and both feet up on the sill, a kettle steaming on the stove beside her, one hand still resting on the lever.
A woman is halfway up the tower ladder with a coil of wire over one shoulder and a mallet swinging at her hip, looking up past her own hands at the work waiting above her.
Two crew are knocking the ice off a cable with long-handled mallets, swinging in turn, and the shards are flying off and away down into the fog underneath them.
A boy has come up through the roof hatch at a dead sprint with both arms full of coiled wire and is skidding sideways on the wet leads, grinning, about to go down.
An old signaller is sitting on the parapet edge with both legs hanging over the street, a splice across his lap and a tar brush in his fist, entirely unbothered by the height.
Three of a crew are hauling on one rope in a row, all three leaning back at the same steep angle with their heels dug in, walking a new cable up off the slates.
A signaller has one foot up on the gallery rail and is reaching far out with a boat-hook to catch a halyard that has blown out of reach, her free hand locked in the lattice.
A woman is lying full length along the roof ridge with her head and shoulders out over the valley gutter and both arms down inside it, working blind at something she cannot see.
Two figures are sharing one lamp on the leads at the foot of the tower, heads almost touching over a coil of wire, one holding the light steady for the other's hands.
A keeper is feeding the pigeons on the tower gallery out of a scoop and the birds are all over the rail, on her shoulders, on her head, and two are in the scoop itself.
A signaller is caught mid-turn, swinging a lever right over with both hands while looking back hard over her shoulder at the far tower to see the answer come.
A crew member is straddling the tower's top crossbar with his legs locked round it and both hands free, threading a wire through a bracket above his own head.
A woman is walking the roof ridge with both arms out for balance and a mallet in one hand, taking the short way across to the next tower.
Two crew have a canvas cradle slung under a cable and one of them is lying in it face-up, working directly above himself, while the other keeps a hand on the cradle rope.
A keeper is flinging a bucket of grit out across the frozen leads ahead of himself and the grit is going absolutely everywhere, including all over his own feet.
A signaller has stopped dead in the middle of a task and is standing quite still with one hand raised flat, head tilted, listening to something.
Four of a crew are eating on the leads at the tower's foot, three of them sat along a coil of wire and one standing, tin mugs balanced on the slates around them.
A woman is hanging off the outside of the tower with one arm hooked through the lattice, laying a fresh white band across a blade with a loaded brush.
A crew is walking a heavy cable drum along the roof on laid planks, four of them shoving at its cheeks and a fifth steering it with an iron bar.
A signaller has a brass telescope up on the gallery rail and is bent right down to it, watching the far tower's blades, one hand shielding the eyepiece from the light.
An apprentice is holding a lamp up as high as she can stretch for a crew member working above her inside the lattice, standing on tiptoe on a slate.
A keeper is down on her knees on the leads with a whole drum's worth of wire flaked out round her in loops, patiently sorting the tangle.
